title: Mechanisms of change in multimodal mental health treatments: The PSYMPACT study
summary:
Mental health conditions are among the leading causes of health problems worldwide. They often result in significant daily challenges and high societal costs. Psychotherapy, medications, and online treatment options (e-mental-health) have proven helpful, but challenges remain: many individuals respond only moderately to treatment, relapse rates are high, and not everyone has access to the support they need.

Most existing research on treatment effectiveness has been conducted under controlled, often standardized conditions that do not fully reflect real-world care settings. This contributes to a gap between research and practice. Furthermore, we still know too little about how and why treatments lead to improvement. For instance, how factors like treatment intensity, the relationship between patient and therapist, or specific techniques interact. Additionally, the links between changes in personality, mental health, and physical health have hardly been explored.

This planned study aims to identify factors contributing to improved mental and physical health in different treatment settings. To do this, we will follow approximately 3,000 people over an extended period who are receiving, e.g., psychiatric, psychotherapeutic, or online treatment. We will examine how their psychological symptoms, personality traits, quality of life, and physical stress develop over time. We will also interview individuals experiencing varying levels of distress to understand their experiences and perspectives better.

An additional focus will be placed on physical stress, measured using repeated analyses of cortisol — a stress hormone stored in hair. Additionally, we will use a smartphone-based diary (ecological momentary assessment, EMA) to track how personality changes in daily life and how these changes are linked to treatment outcomes.
conditions: Participants are mainly recruited through the mental health app MindDoc. In a pilot study, we found that over 60% of users seek further treatment such as psychotherapy, medication or DiGas. Furthermore, users show a wide range of mental disorders. The aim of the present study is to link dimensional changes in mental health profiles with treatment modalities and factors influencing their effectiveness.
